data.body:
GAP 5 IS IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED: Gerrit change 1154, commit b872bc3c89.

WIRED: finalize_verdict takes provider_provenance as a keyword and sets the key ONLY when present.
Carried from steps.verify.outputs.provider_provenance in the plan-review coach step and in the
completion gate's completion_reconcile; the coach-failure recovery path reads it from
succeeded[STEP_VERIFY], which that path requires to have succeeded.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN SURVEY: I said the coach step is duplicated across TWO branch arms. It is
FOUR -- the outer verify_branch (agentic vs single-turn verifier) each contains a coach_gate branch
with then/else arms, at roughly lines 242, 262, 341 and 361. Both outer arms define their own verify
step so the reference resolves in all four. All four are wired. Had the contract test asserted "both
arms" by index instead of iterating every arm it found, two would have shipped unwired.

THREE SITES DELIBERATELY PASS NOTHING, with a comment at each: the DET short-circuit and the outage
degrade ran no model, and the verify-failure recovery has no verify outputs by construction.

ONE CHANGE BEYOND THE PLANNED SHAPE, and it is load-bearing. The premise "the key already exists on
the verify step's outputs" holds only for a LIVE runner: findings.finalize_outcome omits it when no
provider resolved, which is every FakeRunner and canned/injected agent, and executor._resolve_one
RAISES on a missing output. Wiring alone broke 18 offline gate tests with "step 'verify' did not
produce output 'provider_provenance'". Fixed in executor._dispatch's agent branch, immediately after
the existing precedent that materializes schema defaults for sparse canned payloads: the key is
defaulted to None when absent. Always-present-but-None reads as "no provider record for this call",
which downstream carries as an ABSENT verdict key -- identical to a runner that stamped nothing.
This was tried in runs.py first and reverted: tests inject AgentStepRunner subclasses directly,
bypassing RunnerAgentStep, so _dispatch is the only seam covering every runner.
Also: completion_reconcile_input.schema.json is additionalProperties:false, so the new input had to
be DECLARED before the wire was accepted. gen_types regenerated types.py byte-identically.
gate_ops sets the key conditionally, not unconditionally, because
test_reconcile_matches_completion_py_tail asserts the workflow output equals completion.py's
bespoke tail exactly and an extra None key broke it.

MUTATIONS, each restored: drop the wire from ONE of the four coach arms -> 1 test fails (partial
wiring is caught). Source the wire from a NON-agent step (steps.decide) -> 2 fail; only an agent
step's outputs are the runner result verbatim, so a scripted-op source would silently wire None
forever. Coach op passes None instead of its input -> 2 fail, including the end-to-end oracle.

THE ORACLE THAT MATTERS: test_a_real_coach_verdict_survives_into_the_sidecar_payload runs the REAL
coach op, takes whatever verdict it returns, and feeds THAT to the REAL build_payload. No hand-built
verdict anywhere in the file. That composition is the production path, and it is the assertion whose
absence let this gap ship green.

GATES: lint clean, typecheck clean, all six generator/parity gates clean with nothing dirty.
Independently re-verified rather than trusting the implementer's report: 641 passed across
tests/unit/workflow + test_plan_review + both provenance files + the gate-dispatch seam, and 131
passed across the completion suites.

LOC after this change, against the 800 cap: workflow_ops.py 794 (was 787), executor.py 791 (was
779), orchestrator.py 661, plan_review_recovery.py 338, gate_ops.py 192. workflow_ops.py now has SIX
lines of headroom and is the file no seam test guards -- flagged on this ticket earlier and now
materially tighter because of this change.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: e951 (linked discovered_from this ticket) for the code-review gate, which has the
identical defect -- finalize.py:244-245 sets model from cfg and never sets provenance, while
code_review/sidecar.py:106 reads it. Deliberately out of this change to keep it reviewable. Its plan
records both dead ends (no recompute, no usage-aggregate route) so the next implementer does not
re-derive them.

NOT CLOSING until 1154 is Verified +1.
